content.text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule exist, and the rule is enabled.

**Dashboard: `EFF-d731bd2c Web logs overview`** (5 panels, default time range last 1 year)
- Total requests (count metric)
- Average bytes per response (average of `bytes`)
- Requests over time (line, date histogram on `@timestamp`)
- Requests by response code (pie, terms on `response.keyword`)
- Top URLs by requests (bar, terms on `url.keyword`)

Link: http://localhost:15601/app/dashboards#/view/eff-d731bd2c-web-logs-overview-90c7f88bd1de

**Alert rule: `EFF-d731bd2c 5xx spike`** (ID `165268c8-425c-43cb-aeb4-2da58938167c`)
- Type `.es-query` on `kibana_sample_data_logs`, time field `@timestamp`
- Runs every 1m; fires when the count of matching documents in the last 5m is greater than 10
- Match filter: `response.keyword` starts with `5`
- Tagged `EFF-d731bd2c`; enabled. Status is `pending` until its first run.

**Choices I made:**
- The `response` field is a string, so "5xx" is a prefix match on `response.keyword` rather than a numeric range.
- The time range is last 1 year, because I did not confirm when the sample data was loaded.
- The rule has no connector, so it records alerts but sends no notifications. No connectors exist in this Kibana.

**Not verified:**
- I did not check the actual response code values or the time span of the data. The `KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY` variable is not set in my shell, and the local Elasticsearch on port 9200 is not reachable, so I could only inspect the field mapping. The dashboard's response-code pie will show the real distribution.
- I have not confirmed that the rule runs without errors. Check its status once it has run for a minute.
